name: Mark Wang
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO/president, WinWay Technology (TWSE: 6515), Kaohsiung
profile: Mark Wang (Wang Chia-huang / 王嘉煌) founded WinWay Technology in 2001 after ~10 years at ASE's test unit Fulgent Electronics. WinWay makes IC test sockets and interfaces (now also MEMS probe cards) for clients incl. ASE, Nvidia and AMD; listed on TWSE in 2021, its shares surged with AI demand in 2026 and it is building a new plant in Renwu, Kaohsiung.
interesting_fact: WinWay started as a one-man company in Wang's Kaohsiung home with NT$2 million; it is now one of the world's top-five high-end logic IC test socket makers with ~1,200 staff, and its share price passed NT$10,000 in April 2026.
deep_cut_fact: A Chung Yuan University mechanical-engineering grad (not an EE), Wang says the test socket used when Motorola brought its first BGA-packaged chip to Fulgent was his invention. WinWay's break came in 2002 when ATI asked it to build 10 sockets in one week after a foreign supplier failed; he delivered on time.
notes: Romanized variously as Chia-Huang / Jiahuang Wang. The input's SEC insider link to Hilton Grand Vacations is a different Mark Wang (HGV CEO), not this person. Gives interviews to Taiwanese financial media (Mirror Media, Business Today, UDN).

name: Michael Mente
current_role: Co-founder, co-CEO and director, Revolve Group (NYSE: RVLV)
profile: Michael Mente co-founded Revolve with Mike Karanikolas in 2003 using about $50,000 of their savings; the LA-area online fashion retailer pioneered influencer marketing and went public in 2019. As co-CEO he oversees merchandising, brand and the customer experience, including owned brands and the Revolve Festival events.
interesting_fact: Neither founder had a fashion background — both came from a software startup (NextStrat). Mente: 'We don't have fashion backgrounds—we were in tech.' They were named 2015 EY Entrepreneurs of the Year (retail).
deep_cut_fact: Mente left USC's business program in 2000, a year early, to join enterprise-software firm NextStrat, where he met future co-founder Mike Karanikolas.
notes: IR contact listed in Revolve press releases (SVP IR Erik Randerson). Media contact in older releases was the agency Walker Drawas; not re-verified for 2026.

name: Chen Yin
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Greenworks (Jiangsu) Co. (SZSE: 301260)
profile: Chen Yin founded Greenworks (Globe Tools) in Changzhou in 2002; it makes battery-powered lawn, garden and DIY tools sold under Greenworks and other brands, with factories in China, the U.S. and Vietnam. It listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in February 2023; Chen controls a majority stake and still runs the company as chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: Chen is an outspoken advocate of replacing gas-powered outdoor equipment with batteries, arguing operators spend about $4 on electricity for every $100 they would spend on fuel; Greenworks launched its first lithium-ion string trimmer in 2007.
deep_cut_fact: Chen was named EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2016 China in the industrial products category. He studied engineering at Donghua University (formerly China Textile University) and earned an MBA at Warwick.
notes: IR email is from the 2024 interim report; the board secretary is now Li Yirui (per May 2026 earnings-call record). Chen gives occasional English-language trade-press interviews, so US Greenworks PR is a possible route.

name: Kelly Lee
current_role: Chairman (since Dec 2020) and CEO (since Mar 2021), Lungyen Life Service Corp. (TPEx: 5530), Taiwan
profile: Kelly Lee (李凱莉) is the elder daughter of Lee Shih-tsung, founder of Lungyen, Taiwan's leading funeral, cemetery and columbarium services group. She succeeded him as chairman in December 2020 and as CEO in 2021, becoming the largest individual shareholder, and now runs the listed company's funeral services, columbaria and pre-need contract businesses.
interesting_fact: Lungyen is one of the few publicly listed 'death care' companies in Asia; Lee took the chair in a planned succession in December 2020 and spent her first month meeting every department head to learn the business.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal interviews found. Taiwanese coverage of the succession dwells on family matters — avoid. Investor relations page: https://www.lyls.com.tw/sitepage/investorrelations (no email published).

name: Jiang Chun
current_role: Chairman, Anhui Truchum Advanced Materials & Technology (Chujiang New Materials, SZSE: 002171), Wuhu
profile: Jiang Chun (姜纯), born 1960 in Wuhu, has spent 40+ years in copper processing. He built Truchum (楚江新材) into a major maker of copper strip, wire and specialty alloys, later expanding into carbon-fiber composites and high-end equipment via acquisitions; he is the controlling shareholder and chairman.
interesting_fact: Jiang has used acquisitions as Truchum's main growth engine, steering a traditional copper-processing business into advanced materials such as carbon-fiber composites for aerospace.
deep_cut_fact: A metal-forming (压力加工) graduate of Jiangxi Institute of Metallurgy, Jiang joined the newly founded Wuhu Nonferrous Metal Rolling Mill in 1986 and became its director in 1991 at age 31, turning the near-bankrupt plant profitable.
notes: Board-office email listed in the 2024 annual report. Rarely gives interviews; Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Gu Yi
current_role: Probably = Tieer Gu (顾铁), founder, chairman and GM of iRay Technology (SSE STAR: 688301), Shanghai — unconfirmed
profile: Hurun (2021-22) lists '顾轶 / Gu Yi' as the iRay fortune, but no iRay director or shareholder by that name could be found. iRay's founder and actual controller is Tieer Gu (顾铁), who co-founded the X-ray flat-panel detector maker with Cao Hongguang, Qiu Chengbin and Yang Weizhen; the Hurun entry is likely a mis-rendering of his name.
notes: Identity unresolved: verify whether Gu Yi = Tieer Gu before outreach. Contact is iRay's company IR address (2025 annual-report summary).

name: Huang Haoyun
profile: Listed on the Hurun China 2026 list (黄浩云, 'Victory', electrical equipment, ~US$820m). Several Chinese and English searches found no company or filing linking this name to a 'Victory' business; the best-known Victory company (Victory Giant Technology, 胜宏科技, a PCB maker) is run by Chen Tao, and no link to Huang was found.
notes: Could not identify the person or company. Check the Hurun 2026 list entry for the full company name before doing any research or outreach.

name: John Kirkland
profile: John Kirkland OBE, former chairman of the Derbyshire builder Bowmer & Kirkland (founded 1923 by his grandfather Robert Kirkland and Alfred Bowmer), died in November 2021 aged 83. The family's fortune continues to be listed in the Sunday Times Rich List as 'the Kirkland family'.
notes: Deceased (Nov 2021) per Construction Enquirer: https://constructionenquirer.com/2021/11/15/former-bommer-kirkland-chairman-dies . Bowmer & Kirkland remains family-owned; any outreach would be to the next generation via the company.

name: Shantaben Karsanbhai Patel
current_role: Member of the Nirma Group founding family (wife of founder Karsanbhai Patel, per her name); no active executive role found
profile: Shantaben Patel appears on rich lists via a stake in the Nirma Group, the Ahmedabad conglomerate (detergents, soaps, cement, soda ash, pharma) founded in 1969 by Karsanbhai Patel. Nirma began as a one-man after-office business selling cheap detergent door-to-door and became a national brand that undercut multinationals.
interesting_fact: Nirma started in 1969 with Karsanbhai Patel making detergent in his backyard and cycling through Ahmedabad neighbourhoods selling it at Rs 3/kg, about one-third the price of leading brands.
notes: Very private; no public profile or interviews found. Her role and relation are inferred from the listing name, not confirmed by a source. Company general address only. The web-search budget ran out for this item, so verification is limited.

name: Sagar Chordia
current_role: Listed with Panchshil Realty (Pune); exact title unverified (Panchshil's site names Atul Chordia as chairman)
profile: Sagar Chordia is listed as a source of wealth tied to Panchshil Realty, the Pune luxury and commercial developer founded in 2002 by Atul Chordia. Its projects include the EON Free Zone and World Trade Center Pune, Trump Towers Pune and yoopune (with Philippe Starck). Its hospitality arm Ventive Hospitality (a JV with Blackstone) listed in India in December 2024.
interesting_fact: Panchshil's 2010 yoopune residences were designed with Philippe Starck and John Hitchcox's YOO group, and the firm brought Marriott's Courtyard brand to Pune the same year.
notes: Could not confirm his title from a source after the web-search budget ran out. Commonly reported as Atul Chordia's son and a Panchshil director; verify before outreach. The IR email is for affiliate Ventive Hospitality.

name: Yao Wenchen
current_role: Founder and co-controlling shareholder (≈6.4% direct stake) of Shanghai Yaoji Technology (SZSE: 002605); no longer chairman
profile: Yao Wenchen (姚文琛) founded the Yaoji playing-card business (listed in 2011 as Yaoji Poker, now Yaoji Technology), China's leading playing-card maker. The company has since moved into casual mobile games and marketing services. Yao and his family remain the controlling shareholders; day-to-day leadership has passed to the next generation.
interesting_fact: Yaoji is the leader in China's playing-card industry and is building a production base for 600 million decks a year, while most of its profit now comes from casual mobile games.
notes: Profile is based on the 2025 annual report; the web-search budget ran out before founder-story sources could be found. Likely low public profile; outreach via the company board office.

name: Liu Cuiying
current_role: Director, deputy general manager and CFO, Shenzhen Jieshun Science & Technology (SZSE: 002609)
profile: Liu Cuiying (刘翠英, b. 1957) co-owns Jieshun, the Shenzhen smart-parking and access-control company founded in 1992 by her husband Tang Jian, the controlling shareholder. She joined as finance manager in 1997, was CFO until 2018, has been a director since 2010, and is now deputy GM and head of finance.
interesting_fact: Jieshun, which began making parking-lot barrier and access-control systems, now runs smart-parking platforms and works with universities such as Harbin Institute of Technology on AI and large-model parking tech.
deep_cut_fact: With founder Tang Jian she set up the Shenzhen Jieshun Leshan Poverty Alleviation Foundation, which runs scholarship ('爱心助学'), winter-relief and rural-school book and 'little desk' (爱心小书桌) projects.
notes: Hurun lists the fortune jointly with Tang Jian. Sources are the 2025 annual report (director bios, ESG section).

name: Guo Xueyan
current_role: Co-actual controller and shareholder (~6.35%), Shanghai Yongguan Adhesive Products / Yongguan New Materials (SSE: 603681)
profile: Guo Xueyan (郭雪燕, b. 1975) is co-actual controller, with Lyu Xinmin, of Yongguan New Materials (永冠新材), a Shanghai maker of adhesive tapes and films founded in 2002 and listed in Shanghai in 2019. She previously served as finance manager and head of finance at Shanghai Yongguan Adhesive Products.
interesting_fact: Yongguan grew out of a small tape factory in Cangnan county, Zhejiang; co-founder Lyu Xinmin ran the Cangnan Andeli tape factory before setting up Yongguan in Shanghai in 2002.
notes: Holds no current executive post per the 2025 annual report; Lyu Xinmin is chairman and GM. Very low profile. The web-search budget ran out, so the sources are company filings only.

name: Sun Qian
current_role: Former co-controlling shareholder (with Shen Guangqian) of Beijing Leadman Biochemistry (SZSE: 300289); no current role found
profile: Sun Qian (孙茜) and Shen Guangqian were the founding controllers of Leadman (利德曼), a Beijing in-vitro diagnostics reagent and instrument maker listed on ChiNext in 2012 (Hurun China 2012-2017). Leadman is now controlled by a Guangzhou Development District state-owned group; Sun and Shen appear in its 2025 annual report only as parties to legacy IPO and restructuring undertakings.
notes: No longer tied to Leadman management; no current public contact found. Leadman's 2025 annual report (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-03-31/1225051924.PDF) names the state-owned controller. The web-search budget ran out, so current activities were not researched.

name: Yi Dinghong
current_role: Director and president of Beijing Huatu Hongyang Education (Huatu Education); co-actual controller of Huatu Cendes (SZSE: 300492)
profile: Yi Dinghong (易定宏, b. 1969, PhD) co-founded Huatu Education (华图教育) with Wu Jingyu; it is one of China's largest prep providers for civil-service and public-sector exams. He was chairman and GM of Huatu Hongyang from 2011 to 2015 and is now its director and president. Through Huatu Hongyang he controls the Shenzhen-listed Huatu Cendes (华图山鼎), formerly an architecture-design firm.
interesting_fact: Huatu bought control of the listed architecture firm Shanding Design (山鼎设计) and renamed it Huatu Cendes, using it as a vehicle to move into education.
notes: Hurun lists the fortune jointly with Wu Jingyu. The 2025 annual report discloses 2025 court consumption-restriction orders against Yi and Wu tied to investor disputes, so be aware before outreach. Contact is the listed company's board office.

name: Li Xianyu
current_role: Executive director and GM of Double Dove Group (双鸽集团); actual controller of Chimin Health Management (SSE: 603222)
profile: Li Xianyu (李仙玉) controls Double Dove Group of Taizhou, Zhejiang, which owns about 23% of Chimin Health Management (formerly Zhejiang Chimin Pharmaceutical), a maker of infusion products, syringes and other medical consumables listed in Shanghai in 2015. His family are the ultimate controllers, and he also serves on Chimin's board.
interesting_fact: Chimin's Double Dove-brand syringes have been on the market for over 30 years and won 'China Famous Brand' status.
deep_cut_fact: Double Dove Group began in 1984 as the Huangyan County Chengguan Plastic Color-Printing Factory, became the Huangyan Medical Equipment Factory, and was restructured in 1994 into a company led by Li Xianyu.
notes: Filings write his name as 李仙玉. Low media profile; outreach via the Chimin board office.

name: Yu Jianqiu
current_role: Founder, chairman, CEO and executive director, China Metal Resources Utilization Ltd (HKEX: 1636)
profile: Yu Jianqiu (俞建秋, b. c.1964) founded China Metal Resources Utilization (CMRU), a Sichuan-based maker of recycled copper products (copper semis) listed in Hong Kong in 2014; he is its major shareholder through Epoch Keen. Earlier he built Gushan Environmental Energy, a Chinese biodiesel producer, founding several Gushan subsidiaries between 1996 and 2008.
interesting_fact: He chaired Gushan Environmental Energy, one of the first Chinese biodiesel makers with NYSE-listed ADSs (Dec 2007 to Oct 2012), before moving into copper recycling.
deep_cut_fact: Yu earned an Executive MBA from HEC Paris (conferred 13 December 2010) and in 2002 was elected to the Fuzhou committee of the CPPCC; his career spans petrochemicals, automobiles and renewable energy.
notes: Good fit for an energy podcast (biodiesel pioneer, then metal recycling). CMRU shares were suspended in 2023 pending delayed accounts, so check current listing status. The IR email is attention Corporate Communications (HK office).

name: Shen Xinfang
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (~32%) and chief advisor, Zhejiang Tony Electronic (Tonytech, SSE: 603595, now 'ST Dongni'); former chairman
profile: Shen Xinfang (沈新芳) founded Zhejiang Tony Electronic (东尼电子) in Huzhou and controls it with Shen Xiaoyu. Tonytech makes ultra-fine electronic wire and wireless-charging shielding materials for consumer electronics, flexible circuits and battery tabs for EVs, diamond wire for cutting silicon, and silicon-carbide crystal ingots and substrates. He stepped down as chairman and is now the company's chief advisor.
interesting_fact: Tonytech has moved from fine wire for electronics into power-semiconductor materials, growing silicon-carbide single-crystal ingots and substrates, and makes the diamond wire used to slice silicon wafers for solar.
notes: Relevant to energy and semiconductors (SiC, PV diamond wire). The company is under 'ST' risk warning after a Zhejiang CSRC penalty over false disclosures naming the then-chairman, and his shares are partly pledged (2025 annual report). Approach with care.
